members.name: pdh_pdl_fakeout_v141
members.thesis: Previous Day High/Low are obvious technical levels where retail traders place stop losses. Institutional players often drive price just beyond these levels to trigger stops (liquidity hunt) before reversing. Exists due to predictable stop placement.
weaknesses: A True breakout with heavy volume will obliterate this strategy
Slippage can be high right at the liquidity sweep
Requires quick execution as the reversal happens rapidly

members.name: prev_day_hl_reversal
members.thesis: Exploits 'liquidity hunting' at major pivots. The Previous Day High (PDH) and Low (PDL) are significant levels where retail traders place stop orders. Price often 'tags' these levels, executes the stops (liquidity grab), and then reverses. Institutional algos fade these moves once liquidity is tappe
weaknesses: Breakouts can turn into strong trends
Level 'piercing' can be deep, hitting the stop loss first

members.name: prev_day_hl_breakout_v1
members.thesis: Previous day's high and low are watched by a wide cross-section of participants (institutional, algorithmic, retail). When price breaks through these levels with volume, it signals conviction and triggers stop orders placed at these levels. The inefficiency exists because stop clusters at PDH/PDL cr
members.exit_stop: 0.3% from entry or back inside PDH/PDL
filters: no entry in first 15 min (wait for stable price) or last 30 min
weaknesses: False breakouts at PDH/PDL are extremely common. Estimated 55-65% of breakouts reverse within 30 bars. 3-bar confirmation helps but reduces risk/reward.
On ranging days (which dominate — ~60% of trading days), price oscillates around PDH/PDL creating whipsaw losses.
The strategy is crowded — PDH/PDL is literally the most basic level every Indian retail trader watches. Stop-hunting around these levels is common.
members.prior_art: Previous day high/low breakout. One of the oldest intraday setups. See: Mark Fisher (Logical Trader), pivot point literature.

members.name: previous_day_high_low_breakout_v1
members.thesis: Previous day's high and low are the most-watched support/resistance levels by both retail and institutional traders. When price breaks these levels with conviction (volume + close beyond level), stop-loss triggers from the prior day's trapped traders create momentum. The inefficiency exists because
entry_long: dist_from_pdh > 5 AND dist_from_pdh < 30 (clean break, not overextended)
filters: no entries in first 15 min or last 30 min
nifty50 trending in same direction as the trade
weaknesses: False breakouts at PDH/PDL are extremely common — 50% win rate means half the time it fails
On inside days (today's range inside yesterday's), PDH/PDL may never be tested
If many stocks break PDH/PDL simultaneously, it's a macro-driven day and edge comes from market direction, not the level
members.prior_art: Previous Day High/Low breakout — Linda Raschke, Mark Fisher. Ancient setup.

members.name: previous_day_hl_breakout_v1
members.thesis: Previous day's high (PDH) and previous day's low (PDL) are key psychological and structural levels. PDH represents the point where all buyers from yesterday are in profit; PDL represents where all buyers are in loss. Breaking above PDH means exceeding yesterday's maximum bullish sentiment — a new-in
members.exit_target: 0.7% from entry (PDH/PDL breaks tend to produce larger moves than intraday level breaks)
members.exit_stop: PDH for longs (if price falls back below PDH, break failed) OR 0.3%
filters: India_VIX < 25; PDH/PDL breaks in panic VIX are less reliable
prefer breaks before 12:00 IST — afternoon breaks have lower follow-through
volume > 2x 20-bar SMA on the break bar
prefer PDH breaks when NIFTY is also trending up (macro tailwind)
weaknesses: PDH/PDL breaks are the most watched levels in intraday trading — maximum crowding risk
3-bar confirmation means entering late; the best entry was on the break bar itself but that has high reversal risk
On inside days (today's range within yesterday's range), both PDH and PDL may be far from current price — no signals
